div.iching.hex.58.advice: The waters scatter and must gather again. Half your company will leave for another road today; choose which ones to follow yourself.
div.iching.hex.59.advice: The bamboo joint limits what passes through. Carry only what you can lift alone past the narrow gate.
div.iching.hex.6.advice: The host must know the ground. Before you travel a new road, send word ahead through a caravanserai runner.
div.iching.hex.60.advice: Inner truth moves even across still water. Follow the route your heart settled on at dawn, even if three merchants warn you away.
div.iching.hex.61.advice: A small excess tips the scale. Take slightly more water than your skin can hold and slightly less coin than you planned to carry.
div.iching.hex.62.advice: You have already crossed the greater part and only the last ford remains. Do not relax at the final station.
div.iching.hex.63.advice: You are not yet across — the far bank is in sight but the boatman is on the other side. Light a fire on the shore and wait for morning.
div.iching.hex.7.advice: Grouping holds the men around a single well. Choose a road where caravans gather; a bare road this month means bandit sign.
div.iching.hex.8.advice: Small restraint gathers strength for the climb. Do not leave today; one more night in this city will put the road in your favour.
div.iching.hex.9.advice: Tread carefully where the path is narrow. The mountain track holds ice in the shadow; let the mule test every step.
div.iching.name: I Ching
div.iching.result.00: This hexagram favours a slow overland march. Ask at the posting station before you plan the route.
div.iching.result.01: The moving lines are many. Reroute to the nearest walled town and rest three days.
div.iching.result.02: The timing and position are against a river crossing. Wait until the wind settles before you wade.
div.iching.result.03: The western road has dense caravans and easy news. Ask about prices but do not buy in haste.
div.iching.result.04: The northern road has strict checkpoints. Prepare your papers and an interpreter first.
div.iching.result.05: The sea monsoon is not yet stable. Take short coast-hugging stages instead.
div.iching.result.06: Travel in company on this leg. If you go alone, ask less often and pause more.
div.iching.result.07: Before the pass, offer a small gift and then ask the hours of passage.
div.iching.result.08: Pack rations for twice the expected days; the dry stretch has no resupply.
div.iching.result.09: Stay briefly in this city. Do not linger haggling — you may lose your weather window.
div.iching.result.10: The post road forks. Take the branch that has a well.
div.iching.result.11: Night travel is not favoured. Set out at first light.
div.iching.result.12: This hexagram advises: learn the tax rules before entering the market.
div.iching.result.13: Among your company is one who knows the road. Ask them to walk ahead.
div.iching.result.14: Lighten the camel train. Do not carry a full load on the mountain path.
div.iching.result.15: The ferry crossing is crowded. Circle upstream to the shallow ford.
div.iching.result.16: On this leg, secure lodging before you open trade.
div.iching.result.17: The wind is turning. Sea-going vessels should wait two more days.
div.iching.result.18: Prices at the border market are inflated. Compare three stalls before you decide.
div.iching.result.19: The gate clerks rotate soon. Pass through while the old rules still stand.
div.iching.result.20: Travel the desert stretch by night and rest by day.
div.iching.result.21: This hexagram favours hiring a guide. Do not trust an old map alone.
div.iching.result.22: The river ice is about to melt. Find a wooden bridge instead of fording.
div.iching.result.23: The city gate closes at dusk. Enter early.
div.iching.result.24: The trade road has reports of robbery. Switch to the official highway.
div.iching.result.25: Carry salt and tea as gifts on this leg; they open doors faster than words.
div.iching.result.26: Post-horses are scarce. Alternate walking and riding stretches.
div.iching.result.27: The rains are coming. Cross the valley before the mud sets in.
div.iching.result.28: This hexagram says: ask about the water source before you choose a campsite.
div.iching.result.29: The destination city has a festival. Enter early to secure an inn.
div.jiaobei.name: Jiaobei
div.jiaobei.result.00: Great fortune: the cups grant leave to ask the road of the next town before you choose.
div.jiaobei.result.01: The cups grant leave to hire a guide for the mountain pass.
div.jiaobei.result.02: The cups grant leave to wait one tide before boarding.
div.jiaobei.result.03: The cups grant leave to buy grain here; the next market will be dearer.
div.jiaobei.result.04: The cups grant leave to speak first at the gate, and plainly.
div.jiaobei.result.05: The cups grant leave to take the inland road; the shore road is watched.
div.jiaobei.result.06: The cups grant leave to join the caravan that leaves at dawn.
div.jiaobei.result.07: The cups grant leave to lodge within walls tonight.
div.jiaobei.result.08: The cups grant leave to change silver before the frontier.
div.jiaobei.result.09: The cups grant leave to ask three prices before you buy.
div.jiaobei.result.10: Great ill omen: the cups refuse the crossing today; seek another ford tomorrow.
div.jiaobei.result.11: The cups refuse night travel; wait for the second watch of morning.
div.jiaobei.result.12: The cups refuse a bargain struck in haste at this stall.
div.jiaobei.result.13: The cups refuse the short desert cut; keep to the wells.
div.jiaobei.result.14: The cups refuse to open a sealed letter on the road.
div.jiaobei.result.15: The cups refuse sailing under this wind; another day.
div.jiaobei.result.16: The cups refuse hiring the loudest guide in the square.
div.jiaobei.result.17: The cups refuse camping without a wall in sight.
div.jiaobei.result.18: The cups refuse paying the first toll named to you.
div.jiaobei.result.19: The cups refuse parting from the company you already have.
div.jiaobei.result.20: The cups laugh: ask again after you have counted your water-skins.
div.jiaobei.result.21: The cups laugh: ask again when the dust settles and you can see the posts.
div.jiaobei.result.22: The cups laugh: ask again once you have spoken to a local scribe.
div.jiaobei.result.23: The cups laugh: ask again after noon prayer when the bazaar thins.
div.jiaobei.result.24: The cups laugh: ask again with a clearer question of one road only.
div.jiaobei.result.25: The cups laugh: ask again after you sleep one night in this city.
div.jiaobei.result.26: The cups laugh: ask again when your companion is sober.
div.jiaobei.result.27: The cups laugh: ask again beside the temple threshold, not in the street.
div.jiaobei.result.28: The cups laugh: ask again after you have named the city you mean.
div.jiaobei.result.29: The cups laugh: ask again; this cast has nothing yet to say.
div.lenormand.name: Lenormand
div.lenormand.result.00: The Rider: news gallops toward you; a message arrives this day.
div.lenormand.result.01: The Clover: a small luck; take the offered discount.
div.lenormand.result.02: The Ship: a voyage; the crossing is favored.
div.lenormand.result.03: The House: a return home; or a safe house on the road.
div.lenormand.result.04: The Tree: health and growth; a companion recovers.
div.lenormand.result.05: The Clouds: confusion; the way is unclear until dawn.
div.lenormand.result.06: The Serpent: a cunning rival; watch the one who smiles too much.
div.lenormand.result.07: The Coffin: an ending; close one account before opening another.
div.lenormand.result.08: The Bouquet: a gift; an invitation to a feast.
div.lenormand.result.09: The Scythe: a sudden cut; end the delay abruptly.
div.lenormand.result.10: The Whip: a quarrel; keep the peace at the market.
div.lenormand.result.11: The Birds: chatter; gossip flies about your goods.
div.lenormand.result.12: The Child: a new beginning; a small start grows.
div.lenormand.result.13: The Fox: a trick; guard the ledger from the sly merchant.
div.lenormand.result.14: The Bear: strength and a patron; seek the elder's support.
div.lenormand.result.15: The Stars: guidance; the road is clear under the night sky.
div.lenormand.result.16: The Stork: a change; a move that improves your lot.
div.lenormand.result.17: The Dog: a faithful friend; the retainer is loyal.
div.lenormand.result.18: The Tower: an authority; the citadel holds your answer.
div.lenormand.result.19: The Garden: a gathering; the fair brings good company.
div.lenormand.result.20: The Mountain: an obstacle; a hard pass, but passable.
div.lenormand.result.21: The Crossroads: a choice; two roads both lead well.
div.lenormand.result.22: The Mice: a small loss; check the sacks for holes.
div.lenormand.result.23: The Heart: affection; a bond strengthens on the journey.
div.lenormand.result.24: The Ring: a contract; the agreement holds.
div.lenormand.result.25: The Book: a secret; a document hides a truth.
div.lenormand.result.26: The Letter: a written word; the missive carries your fortune.
div.lenormand.result.27: The Man: a man of influence aids the journey.
div.lenormand.result.28: The Woman: a woman of influence aids the journey.
div.lenormand.result.29: The Lily: peace and virtue; the road ends in quiet honor.
div.liuyao.name: Six Lines
div.liuyao.result.00: The first line moves: the foundation is sound; begin as planned.
div.liuyao.result.01: The second line holds: a neighbor's help comes at the river.
div.liuyao.result.02: The third line trembles: do not go forward half-prepared.
div.liuyao.result.03: The fourth line yields: a door opens that you thought closed.
div.liuyao.result.04: The fifth line stands firm: the prince of the road favors you.
div.liuyao.result.05: The sixth line turns back: return; the way ahead is not yet ready.
div.liuyao.result.06: A moving line in the money seat: silver will change hands twice before dusk.
div.liuyao.result.07: The officer line is strong: one who holds authority will aid you.
div.liuyao.result.08: The self line is weak: rest before you answer the call.
div.liuyao.result.09: A strong father line: a letter or a guide comes first.
div.liuyao.result.10: The enemy line faces you: do not provoke the argument at the inn.
div.liuyao.result.11: A line of response rises: your question is answered in three days.
div.liuyao.result.12: The god of joy sits on the road: an auspicious journey; laugh as you go.
div.liuyao.result.13: A hidden line in the palace: a secret of the house will surface.
div.liuyao.result.14: The star of calamity appears: a small loss saves a greater one.
div.liuyao.result.15: The line of the tomb seals the plan: delay until the next full moon.
div.liuyao.result.16: A line of the void: what you seek is not where you look; ask again.
div.liuyao.result.17: The changing line opens the road: a gate that was shut now stands ajar.
div.liuyao.result.18: A line of the crown prince: a younger person speaks truth; listen.
div.liuyao.result.19: The line of the servant is weak: do not rely on another's errand.
div.liuyao.result.20: A line of the spouse crosses the travel: a marriage or a bond changes the route.
div.liuyao.result.21: The line of the thunder: act, but expect a sudden turn.
div.liuyao.result.22: A line of the lake: pleasure delays the schedule; keep the watch.
div.liuyao.result.23: The line of the mountain: a barrier holds; wait for the season to turn.
div.liuyao.result.24: A line of wind: news travels fast; your plans are already known.
div.liuyao.result.25: The line of fire: anger flares; keep your temper at the market.
div.liuyao.result.26: A line of water: an obstacle dissolves; the way clears by evening.
div.liuyao.result.27: The line of earth: stability; stay with what you know.
div.liuyao.result.28: A line of the gate: an official checks your papers; have them ready.
div.liuyao.result.29: The six lines settle: the cast is complete; go in peace with its counsel.
div.lot.apprentice: The temple keeper shakes the bamboo cylinder until a single numbered stick clatters onto the stone floor. He picks it up, squints at the number, and turns to a cabinet of a hundred drawers. 'Each lot is a verse,' he says, selecting a slip of paper. 'Each verse is a warning or a permission. The gods do not prophesy — they advise. Learn to hear the difference, and you will never be lost.'
div.lot.desc: Temple lots give a direct answer to a single question — yes or no, with a warning. Shake the bamboo cylinder until one numbered stick falls. The keeper reads the corresponding verse from the book. Best for immediate decisions: Should I take this road today? Is this merchant honest? Cost: 50 coins. Horizon: one day.
div.lot.name: Temple Lots
div.lot.result.00: The lot says: advance along the planned posting stations; do not change the route at the last moment.
div.lot.result.01: The lot says: advance along the planned posting stations; do not change the route at the last moment.
div.lot.result.02: The lot warns: do not board a boat today. Wait for tomorrow's tide.
div.lot.result.03: The lot says: compare the same goods at three stalls before you buy.
div.lot.result.04: The lot says: join a caravan; do not walk the solitary stretch alone.
div.lot.result.05: The lot says: halt at this fork and return to the city for more provisions.
div.lot.result.06: The lot says: leave at dawn to avoid the checkpoint queues.
div.lot.result.07: The lot says: do not camp in the wild tonight; find a walled posting inn.
div.lot.result.08: The lot says: courtesy before questions at the pass shortens the delay.
div.lot.result.09: The lot says: hide your best goods in the market; do not display them.
div.lot.result.10: The lot says: where the tongue is strange, hire an interpreter before you negotiate.
div.lot.result.11: The lot says: two roads run equal; choose the one with wells.
div.lot.result.12: The lot says: wait one full tidal cycle before putting to sea.
div.lot.result.13: The lot says: lighten the load on the mountain road; split the cargo into two trips.
div.lot.result.14: The lot says: if anyone in your party is ill, treat them inside the city before you leave.
div.lot.result.15: The lot says: take the detour. The official road is longer but has fewer robbers.
div.lot.result.16: The lot says: learn the port tax rate before you enter the city.
div.lot.result.17: The lot says: keep your word. Do not delay a promised delivery date again.
div.lot.result.18: The lot says: curb your desire. Buy only what you need of this city's wares.
div.lot.result.19: The lot says: near the sea, visit the shrine to the sea-goddess before you sail.
div.lot.result.20: The lot says: when reports contradict, stop for one day before you decide.
div.lot.result.21: The lot says: travel north. The northern road has steadier resupply.
div.lot.result.22: The lot says: travel south. The monsoon is turning; consider the sea route.
div.lot.result.23: The lot says: travel west. Camel hire is cheap now; arrange your transport.
div.lot.result.24: The lot says: travel east. Documents are easy to obtain; checkpoints are lenient.
div.lot.result.25: The lot says: a short stop. Spend one night only; do not grow fond of the market.
div.lot.result.26: The lot says: a long stay. Learn the local tongue for a season before you move on.
div.lot.result.27: The lot says: a small gift for directions beats an empty word.
div.lot.result.28: The lot says: record the road conditions in your codex for the return journey.
div.lot.result.29: The lot says: ask one question per lot. Do not draw twice on the same day.
div.meihua.name: Plum Blossom
div.meihua.result.00: One plum blossom falls: a single loss marks the beginning; continue.
div.meihua.result.01: Two blossoms: a pairing serves the journey; travel with another.
div.meihua.result.02: Three blossoms: three days of rain; plan for wet roads.
div.meihua.result.03: Four blossoms: four gates; the south gate opens for you.
div.meihua.result.04: Five blossoms: five coins find their way into your purse.
div.meihua.result.05: Six blossoms: six leagues a day; an easy pace.
div.meihua.result.06: Seven blossoms: seven days of waiting at the pass.
div.meihua.result.07: Eight blossoms: eight directions; only one is yours — the east.
div.meihua.result.08: A blossom on the water: what you set afloat returns to you.
div.meihua.result.09: A blossom in the dust: an idea takes root in plain soil.
div.meihua.result.10: The number of the hour: act when the bell strikes; not before.
div.meihua.result.11: The number of the day: the market favors the third day's trading.
div.meihua.result.12: The number of your age: a mature counsel is best; heed the elder.
div.meihua.result.13: The number of the road: count your baggage; one thing too many.
div.meihua.result.14: A blossom caught in a web: a plan entangled; free it slowly.
div.meihua.result.15: A blossom on the threshold: a guest arrives who changes your plans.
div.meihua.result.16: A blossom turning in the wind: direction uncertain; ask twice.
div.meihua.result.17: A blossom at the door of the shrine: a vow is heard; keep your promise.
div.meihua.result.18: A blossom in the morning dew: an early start brings fortune.
div.meihua.result.19: A blossom fallen at noon: a mid-course change is wise.
div.meihua.result.20: A blossom at dusk: an evening errand should wait for daylight.
div.meihua.result.21: A blossom among the reeds: a hidden path reveals itself.
div.meihua.result.22: A blossom on the cart wheel: the journey turns upon a small choice.
div.meihua.result.23: A blossom beside the fire: warmth and kinship; seek the hearth.
div.meihua.result.24: A blossom carried by the bird: news from afar alights with you.
div.meihua.result.25: A blossom in the rain: tears and relief; the storm passes.
div.meihua.result.26: A blossom on the altar: a promise made in haste; bind it well.
div.meihua.result.27: A blossom under the moon: a secret journey is guarded.
div.meihua.result.28: A blossom on the ledger: a debt is recorded; settle it.
div.meihua.result.29: A blossom in the closing hand: the cast closes; accept the answer.
div.numerology.name: Numerology
div.numerology.result.00: The number one: a beginning; set out on the first day of the week.
div.numerology.result.01: The number two: a partnership; find your counterpart before the gate.
div.numerology.result.02: The number three: a trinity of days; travel a short way, then rest.
div.numerology.result.03: The number four: a square foundation; the road is solid but slow.
div.numerology.result.04: The number five: the crossroads; choose, for the road will not wait.
div.numerology.result.05: The number six: balance and care; the market rewards patience.
div.numerology.result.06: The number seven: mystery; a secret path opens at the seventh hour.
div.numerology.result.07: The number eight: infinity; the journey turns back on itself; see it through.
div.numerology.result.08: The number nine: completion; what you finish here blesses the next stage.
div.numerology.result.09: A doubled number: haste doubles the error; slow down.
div.numerology.result.10: A sum of eleven: mastery; a skill you learned serves you now.
div.numerology.result.11: A sum of twelve: the wheel of the year; wait for the season's turn.
div.numerology.result.12: A sum of thirteen: change; a sudden turn hides a gift.
div.numerology.result.13: A sum of fourteen: the moon waxes; a quiet plan comes to light.
div.numerology.result.14: A sum of fifteen: the weaver's number; what is woven will hold.
div.numerology.result.15: A sum of sixteen: the tower; a structure falls so a new one may rise.
div.numerology.result.16: A sum of seventeen: the star; your hope shines over the road.
div.numerology.result.17: A sum of eighteen: the moon darkens; keep your counsel tonight.
div.numerology.result.18: A sum of nineteen: the sun returns; a fresh day for your venture.
div.numerology.result.19: A number in your name: your own name opens the gate.
div.numerology.result.20: A number of your city: the town's fortune walks with you.
div.numerology.result.21: A number of your birth: the year of your birth favors this road.
div.numerology.result.22: A count of your cargo: an odd count brings luck to the sale.
div.numerology.result.23: A count of your coin: an even count spends well at the fair.
div.numerology.result.24: A count of your days: the number of days to the pass is auspicious.
div.numerology.result.25: A count of the stars: follow the count of the morning stars.
div.numerology.result.26: A number from a stranger: trust the sum he names, nothing more.
div.numerology.result.27: A number from the shrine: the offering the gods accept.
div.numerology.result.28: A number from a dream: the dream number guides the morning choice.
div.numerology.result.29: A number that repeats: what returns once will return again; be ready.
div.oracle.name: Oracle Cards
div.oracle.result.00: The Open Gate: an opportunity stands ajar; enter.
div.oracle.result.01: The Closed Gate: a door is shut; do not force it.
div.oracle.result.02: The Lantern: guidance; follow the light of an old custom.
div.oracle.result.03: The Mirror: reflection; look to your own conduct.
div.oracle.result.04: The Compass: direction; your sense of the way is true.
div.oracle.result.05: The Anchor: stability; hold your course.
div.oracle.result.06: The Sail: movement; the wind favors departure.
div.oracle.result.07: The Bell: a warning; a summons to attention.
div.oracle.result.08: The Feather: lightness; a burden lifts from you.
div.oracle.result.09: The Key: an answer; the lock yields to patience.
div.oracle.result.10: The Shield: protection; a defense stands ready.
div.oracle.result.11: The Arrow: a direct aim; the plan strikes true.
div.oracle.result.12: The Nest: a safe place; the inn shelters you.
div.oracle.result.13: The Spring: a source; refreshment at the well.
div.oracle.result.14: The Path: a way is shown; follow it simply.
div.oracle.result.15: The Thorn: a small hurt; remove it early.
div.oracle.result.16: The Flame: passion; let it burn, but guard the storehouse.
div.oracle.result.17: The Stone: endurance; the heavy step is necessary.
div.oracle.result.18: The Hourglass: time; the sand runs; decide.
div.oracle.result.19: The Crown: honor; a position is offered.
div.oracle.result.20: The Coin: value; the trade is fair.
div.oracle.result.21: The Dawn: a new day; the morning is propitious.
div.oracle.result.22: The Dusk: an ending; conclude the day's work.
div.oracle.result.23: The Cloud: a veiling; wait for clearer sight.
div.oracle.result.24: The Rainbow: a promise; what was lost is restored.
div.oracle.result.25: The Wind: change; an unseen force moves your plans.
div.oracle.result.26: The Earth: grounded; a plain answer to a plain question.
div.oracle.result.27: The Sky: vast possibility; do not limit the journey.
div.oracle.result.28: The Silence: no answer yet; ask again at the next city.
div.oracle.result.29: The Voice: a call; a purpose finds you on this road.
div.palmistry.name: Palmistry
div.palmistry.result.00: The life line runs long: many leagues await; do not hurry them.
div.palmistry.result.01: The life line breaks: a rest is needed; stop at the next river.
div.palmistry.result.02: The life line curves wide: a wide journey; far cities call.
div.palmistry.result.03: The life line runs close: a cautious road; keep to the beaten track.
div.palmistry.result.04: The head line is straight: a direct mind; the plan is clear.
div.palmistry.result.05: The head line slopes: a dreaming mind; guard the purse.
div.palmistry.result.06: The head line is deep: a firm decision; the road bends to it.
div.palmistry.result.07: The head line is faint: an uncertain mind; ask twice.
div.palmistry.result.08: The heart line rises: an open heart; friendship comes easily.
div.palmistry.result.09: The heart line descends: a guarded heart; keep counsel.
div.palmistry.result.10: The heart line is long: loyalty; the companion is true.
div.palmistry.result.11: The heart line is short: a quick affection; a quick parting.
div.palmistry.result.12: The fate line is strong: a destined road; follow it without doubt.
div.palmistry.result.13: The fate line is broken: a change of course; the new way is better.
div.palmistry.result.14: The fate line begins at the wrist: a road from humble start to high end.
div.palmistry.result.15: The fate line begins at the palm: a road chosen freely; take it.
div.palmistry.result.16: The sun line shines: fame at the next city; accept the honor.
div.palmistry.result.17: The sun line is absent: a quiet journey; wealth unspoken.
div.palmistry.result.18: The mount of the thumb is full: strength; the heavy load is yours to carry.
div.palmistry.result.19: The mount of the forefinger is full: ambition; aim at the chief's seat.
div.palmistry.result.20: The mount of the middle finger is full: caution; count the coin twice.
div.palmistry.result.21: The mount of the ring finger is full: art; a craft will pay the way.
div.palmistry.result.22: The mount of the little finger is full: speech; a word well placed opens gates.
div.palmistry.result.23: The bracelets are deep: long years and a long road.
div.palmistry.result.24: A star on the mount of the moon: a sea voyage; a crossing is blessed.
div.palmistry.result.25: A cross on the mount of Jupiter: a marriage or a meeting of import.
div.palmistry.result.26: A triangle on the head line: a clever bargain; sign it.
div.palmistry.result.27: A square on the life line: protection; a shield follows you.
div.palmistry.result.28: Many fine lines: a busy road; many small dealings.
div.palmistry.result.29: The heart and head lines meet: a single will; your choice is the right one.
div.qimen.name: Qi Men Dun Jia
div.qimen.result.00: The Door of Life opens at the first watch: depart before the rooster crows.
div.qimen.result.01: The Door of Rest holds the second day: linger and mend your gear.
div.qimen.result.02: The Heavenly Stem reaches the gate: a senior will speak; heed the words.
div.qimen.result.03: A hidden gate in the northwest: a shortcut exists, but only at dawn.
div.qimen.result.04: The Earth Door is shut: the road is watched; take the market road instead.
div.qimen.result.05: The Door of Sickness shows in the chart: keep the invalid's goods off your cart.
div.qimen.result.06: A white bird crosses the gate: a message arrives by courier this week.
div.qimen.result.07: The Five Ghosts drift toward the road: travel with bells to keep them away.
div.qimen.result.08: The Gate of Fortune opens at the third watch: buy your goods before the noon crowd.
div.qimen.result.09: A flying star rests on the crossroads: ask twice before you choose the fork.
div.qimen.result.10: The Door of Death lies on the south road: do not go that way for seven days.
div.qimen.result.11: A mystic gate appears at the hour of the horse: what is lost will be found.
div.qimen.result.12: The Heavenly Secret is visible: keep your route quiet until you pass the custom post.
div.qimen.result.13: A red cloud covers the gate: a storm delays you; shelter in the caravanserai.
div.qimen.result.14: The Gate of Long Life opens at the fifth watch: a trusted companion brings good news.
div.qimen.result.15: The Nine Palaces turn: your plan is sound but the timing is off — wait a day.
div.qimen.result.16: A locked gate in the chart: a document is needed; ask for it at the citadel.
div.qimen.result.17: The stars form a bridge: a safe crossing lies upstream; seek it.
div.qimen.result.18: A gate ajar to the east: a trading partner waits; go and settle the price.
div.qimen.result.19: The Heavenly Sword points home: return by the way you came; it is safest.
div.qimen.result.20: A low gate at noon: do not negotiate while the sun is high.
div.qimen.result.21: The Door of Industry opens: a craft will earn your passage at the next town.
div.qimen.result.22: A wandering star enters the gate: news of a lost friend reaches you here.
div.qimen.result.23: The Gate of Slaughter is quiet: what you feared is past; go in peace.
div.qimen.result.24: A threefold gate: three ways are open; the middle holds your fortune.
div.qimen.result.25: The Earth moves under the gate: a delay on the road, but no harm.
div.qimen.result.26: A gate lit by fire: a quarrel over coin; keep your ledger ready.
div.qimen.result.27: The Door of Justice opens at dusk: a dispute over goods will end in your favor.
div.qimen.result.28: A banner before the gate: join the caravan bound for the eastern city.
div.qimen.result.29: The gate stands open at midnight: a secret errand may be done unnoticed.
div.runes.name: Runes
div.runes.result.00: Great fortune: the rune names company — join the next wagon before the steppe widens.
div.runes.result.01: The rune names a river crossing at dawn, when the ice is still firm.
div.runes.result.02: The rune names speaking the northern tongue at the next post.
div.runes.result.03: The rune names a gift of salt to the first elder who greets you.
div.runes.result.04: The rune names marking the stars for three nights before you turn.
div.runes.result.05: The rune names keeping your sword visible but sheathed in this town.
div.runes.result.06: The rune names buying felt and not silk on this market day.
div.runes.result.07: The rune names a detour to the wooden church for news of the road.
div.runes.result.08: The rune names waiting out the blizzard in the stockaded yard.
div.runes.result.09: The rune names hiring a local boy who knows the wolf tracks.
div.runes.result.10: The rune names delay: one day for the ferry ropes to be mended.
div.runes.result.11: The rune names delay until the tribute train has passed.
div.runes.result.12: The rune names delay: dry your boots before the next marsh.
div.runes.result.13: Ill omen: the rune names danger on the reed bank; keep to the raised track.
div.runes.result.14: The rune names danger in the abandoned tower; do not shelter there.
div.runes.result.15: The rune names danger if you travel without a bell on the lead horse.
div.runes.result.16: The rune names an ally among the fur traders of this quay.
div.runes.result.17: The rune names an ally if you share bread at the gate-fire.
div.runes.result.18: The rune names travel light across the frozen lake; leave the cart.
div.runes.result.19: The rune names travel with the amber merchants bound west.
div.runes.result.20: The rune names travel only while the sun clears the pine line.
div.runes.result.21: The rune names holding your question until you reach the next idol-post.
div.runes.result.22: The rune names holding silver back from the first inn's reckoning.
div.runes.result.23: The rune names holding the southern fork; the northern is flooded.
div.runes.result.24: The rune names asking the Varangian guard which bridge still stands.
div.runes.result.25: The rune names writing the tribal passwords you are given tonight.
div.runes.result.26: The rune names not racing the horse that limps into the yard.
div.runes.result.27: The rune names counting your arrows before you leave the stockade.
div.runes.result.28: The rune names paying the ferryman what he asks; argue later ashore.
div.runes.result.29: The rune names turning back one station if the sky turns iron-grey.
div.scrying.name: Scrying
div.scrying.result.00: A white cloud in the glass: a gentle road; the way is mild.
div.scrying.result.01: A red thread: a connection; someone thinks of you.
div.scrying.result.02: A silver river: a crossing; a journey over water.
div.scrying.result.03: A golden gate: a reward; the end of the road holds treasure.
div.scrying.result.04: A dark tower: a warning; keep from that place.
div.scrying.result.05: A green hill: a rest; a village of comfort ahead.
div.scrying.result.06: A blue flame: a passion; a bold choice.
div.scrying.result.07: A grey mist: uncertainty; wait for clarity.
div.scrying.result.08: A black bird: a message; a raven's news, mixed.
div.scrying.result.09: A white horse: speed; a fast errand succeeds.
div.scrying.result.10: A pair of eyes: a witness; you are observed.
div.scrying.result.11: A long road: a long journey; patience is the fare.
div.scrying.result.12: A broken bridge: an interruption; mend the plan.
div.scrying.result.13: A crown of light: honor; a public favor.
div.scrying.result.14: A staff: support; an elder guides you.
div.scrying.result.15: A shadow passing: a spirit; do no ill, take no ill.
div.scrying.result.16: A face in the glass: a meeting; one you know approaches.
div.scrying.result.17: A letter on the water: news afloat; a message delayed.
div.scrying.result.18: A key turning: an answer; the lock yields.
div.scrying.result.19: A moon over a tower: a night vigil; watch till dawn.
div.scrying.result.20: A rain of sparks: a festival; joy at the next town.
div.scrying.result.21: A serpent coiling: a slow poison; cut the tie.
div.scrying.result.22: A flower opening: a gift; a kindness given.
div.scrying.result.23: A mountain parting: a pass opens; the barrier falls.
div.scrying.result.24: A bell ringing: a call; an invitation.
div.scrying.result.25: A ship on a calm sea: a safe voyage; embark.
div.scrying.result.26: A tree in fruit: abundance; the season is rich.
div.scrying.result.27: A veil drawn: a mystery; the truth waits.
div.scrying.result.28: A hand reaching: an offer; accept it.
div.scrying.result.29: The glass darkens: rest; the vision is done for now.

div.tarot.name: Tarot
div.tarot.result.00: The spread points to a steady road. Take the exit with clear resupply.
div.tarot.result.01: A blocking card warns: the shortcut costs more than the official road.
div.tarot.result.02: The resource card sits on the left. Westbound caravans can lend you strength.
div.tarot.result.03: The resource card sits on the right. Eastbound posting stations are more reliable.
div.tarot.result.04: The timeline shows past delays. Shorten today's stage.
div.tarot.result.05: The present card demands: settle your interpreter before you discuss the route.
div.tarot.result.06: The future card opens: within three days, the sea route becomes favourable.
div.tarot.result.07: Door A brings high profit at the cost of time — choose it when your cargo is urgent.
div.tarot.result.08: Door B costs coin but spares time — avoid it when your purse is lean.
div.tarot.result.09: The principle card: let safety outweigh profit on this leg.
div.tarot.result.10: A reversed blockage: do not sign a long hire contract today.
div.tarot.result.11: A reversed excess: do not fill your cargo hold all at once.
div.tarot.result.12: Upright passage: answer the checkpoint questions truthfully.
div.tarot.result.13: A shadow card: do not trust a guide with no known origin.
div.tarot.result.14: The environment card: this city is full of rumour; cross-check every report.
div.tarot.result.15: The self card: the rhythm of the overland road suits you better.
div.tarot.result.16: The outcome card: test the short road before you commit to the long one.
div.tarot.result.17: The challenge card: the river crossing is this leg's key risk.
div.tarot.result.18: The hope card: you can learn a new divination method at the next city.
div.tarot.result.19: The fear card: do not abandon a known road because of a rumour.
div.tarot.result.20: The career spread reads: first secure your position, then seek opportunity.
div.tarot.result.21: The coin-flow points: your costs are in tariffs, not in transport hire.
div.tarot.result.22: The relationship mirror: hear your companions' opinions, but the choice stays yours.
div.tarot.result.23: One-card calibration: the watchword is hold fast, not charge ahead.
div.tarot.result.24: One-card calibration: the watchword is ask first, not buy first.
div.tarot.result.25: The three-card counsel: check the water level before you reroute.
div.tarot.result.26: The Celtic-cross outcome: the long line still points to your original destination.
div.tarot.result.27: Card combination: water dominates; choose roads near rivers and lakes.
div.tarot.result.28: Card combination: fire dominates; avoid marching under the midday sun.
div.tarot.result.29: Card combination: earth dominates; the dry road can carry heavy cargo.
div.vedic.name: Vedic Astrology
div.vedic.result.00: The Moon in the Rohini lodge: the road is smooth and the carts light.
div.vedic.result.01: The Moon in the Ashwini lodge: a fast start; the horse is fresh.
div.vedic.result.02: The Moon in the Pushya lodge: the gods bless the departure; take grain as offering.
div.vedic.result.03: The Moon in the Magha lodge: ancestors guard the road; honor them at the shrine.
div.vedic.result.04: The Moon in the Hasta lodge: skilled hands mend your wheel before the long stretch.
div.vedic.result.05: The Moon in the Swati lodge: a wandering merchant brings news of the eastern fair.
div.vedic.result.06: The Moon in the Mula lodge: a root is pulled up; leave behind what binds you.
div.vedic.result.07: The Moon in the Anuradha lodge: friendship on the road; share your water.
div.vedic.result.08: The Moon in the Uttara Phalguni lodge: a marriage or a feast opens the gate.
div.vedic.result.09: The Moon in the Vishakha lodge: a goal is set; the road bends toward it.
div.vedic.result.10: The Moon in the Jyeshtha lodge: an elder's blessing; seek it before you go.
div.vedic.result.11: The Moon in the Chitra lodge: a bright omen; the craftsman's price is fair.
div.vedic.result.12: The Moon in the Ardra lodge: tears and rain; keep your goods covered.
div.vedic.result.13: The Moon in the Ashlesha lodge: a coiled path; watch for treachery at the inn.
div.vedic.result.14: The Moon in the Punarvasu lodge: a return is blessed; go back with purpose.
div.vedic.result.15: The Moon in the Krttika lodge: a sharp decision; cut cleanly.
div.vedic.result.16: The Moon in the Bharani lodge: a heavy load; a woman's counsel lightens it.
div.vedic.result.17: The Moon in the Uttara Ashadha lodge: an undefeated road; victory at the far gate.
div.vedic.result.18: The Moon in the Purva Ashadha lodge: an old debt is settled on this journey.
div.vedic.result.19: The Moon in the Shravana lodge: listening brings the answer; hear the cry at the well.
div.vedic.result.20: The Moon in the Dhanishta lodge: music and coin; a drummer's rhythm sets the pace.
div.vedic.result.21: The Moon in the Shatabhisha lodge: healing waters; bathe before the crossing.
div.vedic.result.22: The Moon in the Purva Bhadrapada lodge: a restless spirit; keep a lamp burning.
div.vedic.result.23: The Moon in the Uttara Bhadrapada lodge: a steady end; the journey closes well.
div.vedic.result.24: The Moon in the Revati lodge: abundance; the last city offers the best market.
div.vedic.result.25: The Sun enters the sign of the Ram: a new year of the road begins; start strong.
div.vedic.result.26: Rahu stands in the travel house: delay and confusion; double-check the route.
div.vedic.result.27: Ketu stands in the wealth house: what you release returns to you.
div.vedic.result.28: Saturn's transit of the Moon: a heavy heart; move slowly and pray.
div.vedic.result.29: Jupiter watches the journey: the guide you trust is worthy of trust.
div.western.name: Western Astrology
div.western.result.00: The Sun in the first house: the journey begins in your favor.
div.western.result.01: The Moon in the second house: keep your purse close; spending runs high.
div.western.result.02: Mercury in the third house: letters and talk speed your way.
div.western.result.03: Venus in the fourth house: home calls, but the road holds a meeting.
div.western.result.04: Mars in the fifth house: bold play wins at the gaming house; leave before midnight.
div.western.result.05: Jupiter in the sixth house: a servant or hireling proves honest.
div.western.result.06: Saturn in the seventh house: a partnership is tested; sign after the inspection.
div.western.result.07: The Sun in the eighth house: another's goods pass through your hands; guard them.
div.western.result.08: The Moon in the ninth house: a long voyage is blessed by the stars.
div.western.result.09: Mercury in the tenth house: your trade is spoken of; your name opens the gate.
div.western.result.10: Venus in the eleventh house: a friend brings news of a fair.
div.western.result.11: Mars in the twelfth house: an enemy works in shadow; keep counsel.
div.western.result.12: The ascendant in the Bull: move slowly but steadily; the load is heavy.
div.western.result.13: The ascendant in the Twins: two roads; take the one the merchants take.
div.western.result.14: The ascendant in the Crab: the road by the water favors you.
div.western.result.15: The ascendant in the Lion: act like a prince; the town will follow.
div.western.result.16: The ascendant in the Maiden: check your accounts before you sleep.
div.western.result.17: The ascendant in the Scales: weigh the offer; balance the price.
div.western.result.18: The ascendant in the Scorpion: a secret follows the road; do not reveal your goods.
div.western.result.19: The ascendant in the Archer: aim far; the arrow lands well.
div.western.result.20: The ascendant in the Goat: climb slowly; the peak is yours by evening.
div.western.result.21: The ascendant in the Water Bearer: a strange friend brings a stranger gift.
div.western.result.22: The ascendant in the Fishes: follow the current; it leads to the market.
div.western.result.23: Saturn returns: a lesson of the road is repeated; learn it this time.
div.western.result.24: Jupiter ascends: luck grows with each league; share a little.
div.western.result.25: A square of Sun and Moon: a quarrel of two minds; let the elder decide.
div.western.result.26: A trine of Venus and Mars: love and boldness together; a fine bargain.
div.western.result.27: Mercury retrograde: a letter goes astray; re-read what you sign.
div.western.result.28: The Moon in the fortune house: the day is golden; act.
div.western.result.29: A grand cross in the chart: all roads blocked for now; rest, then the stars turn.
div.xiangmian.name: Face Reading
div.xiangmian.result.00: A clear brow: an open road and an open heart; proceed.
div.xiangmian.result.01: A furrowed brow: worry clouds the way; resolve the doubt first.
div.xiangmian.result.02: Bright eyes: a sharp glance finds the best goods at the fair.
div.xiangmian.result.03: Clouded eyes: a deception waits; read the seal twice.
div.xiangmian.result.04: A strong nose: fortune rises with the nose of a prince; negotiate well.
div.xiangmian.result.05: A wide mouth: generous speech earns a discount at the gate.
div.xiangmian.result.06: A thin lip: a tight bargain; give nothing, ask double.
div.xiangmian.result.07: A long chin: endurance; the road is long but you will finish.
div.xiangmian.result.08: A short chin: turn back soon; the plan shortens.
div.xiangmian.result.09: Cheeks that catch the light: the town will remember your face kindly.
div.xiangmian.result.10: Cheeks in shadow: keep your face from the guard's lamp.
div.xiangmian.result.11: A scar across the brow: an old wound speaks; heed its lesson.
div.xiangmian.result.12: A mole at the corner of the eye: a small treasure hides near the road.
div.xiangmian.result.13: A mole on the cheek: a tear and a smile; a mixed fortune.
div.xiangmian.result.14: A mole on the chin: a late reward for a long patience.
div.xiangmian.result.15: A mole on the nose: gossip follows you; ignore it.
div.xiangmian.result.16: Lines at the eyes: laughter lines; seek the tavern's cheer.
div.xiangmian.result.17: Lines at the mouth: years of silence; speak now.
div.xiangmian.result.18: A high forehead: learning; a scholar at the next city will help.
div.xiangmian.result.19: A low forehead: simplicity; an honest deal, but small.
div.xiangmian.result.20: Brows that meet: a tangled road; cut the knot early.
div.xiangmian.result.21: Brows apart: a wide choice; many paths open.
div.xiangmian.result.22: The left eye twitches: a woman brings news.
div.xiangmian.result.23: The right eye twitches: a man brings a quarrel.
div.xiangmian.result.24: A reddened nose: wine and warmth; beware the open purse.
div.xiangmian.result.25: A pale face: illness; rest a day before the pass.
div.xiangmian.result.26: A flushed face: anger; cool it before the bargaining.
div.xiangmian.result.27: A smiling face: the road smiles back; go with cheer.
div.xiangmian.result.28: A downcast face: a heavy heart; unburden it to a friend.
div.xiangmian.result.29: A serene face: peace; the road holds no harm for you.
div.ziwei.name: Zi Wei Dou Shu
div.ziwei.result.00: The Emperor Star holds your chart: command the road; your decisions are sound.
div.ziwei.result.01: The Sun in the palace of travel: a bright season for the road; go with confidence.
div.ziwei.result.02: The Moon dims the travel palace: move by night only when you must.
div.ziwei.result.03: The Chancellor joins the journey: a wise companion offers guidance; accept it.
div.ziwei.result.04: The Great Yang ascends: prosperity on the route; buy and sell boldly.
div.ziwei.result.05: The seven stars cross the wealth palace: cargo sold at the next city yields silver.
div.ziwei.result.06: The Brocade Star shines on the road: a reputation earned here will open gates.
div.ziwei.result.07: A star of misfortune in the travel palace: a minor mishap; spare coin for repairs.
div.ziwei.result.08: The Sky Void enters the chart: what you hope for will not be found here; move on.
div.ziwei.result.09: The Solitary Star sits in the moving palace: travel alone suits you this season.
div.ziwei.result.10: The Tomb Star guards the crossing: keep your goods dry and your words few.
div.ziwei.result.11: The Bride Star in the alliance palace: a marriage offer comes with the trade.
div.ziwei.result.12: The Death Star passes the road palace: end one venture to begin another.
div.ziwei.result.13: The Generals' Star commands your route: a long journey is blessed; plan for many days.
div.ziwei.result.14: The Learning Star brightens: study a new method at the next shrine.
div.ziwei.result.15: The Flame Star burns the wealth palace: spend little at this market.
div.ziwei.result.16: The Water Star calms the journey: a river crossing is safe at low water.
div.ziwei.result.17: The Physician Star attends the party: a sick companion recovers by the next town.
div.ziwei.result.18: The Warrior Star in the palace of the west: guard against thieves on that road.
div.ziwei.result.19: The Wind Star troubles the schedule: allow two days for the mountain stretch.
div.ziwei.result.20: The Inspector Star reviews the route: check your permits before departure.
div.ziwei.result.21: The Gracious Star visits the retainer palace: a companion's loyalty is tested and true.
div.ziwei.result.22: The Crowd Star throngs the market: buy early before prices rise.
div.ziwei.result.23: The Sickle Star reaps the cargo: your goods find a ready buyer at the gate.
div.ziwei.result.24: The Mirror Star reflects the plan: what you arrange now returns to you later.
div.ziwei.result.25: The Cloud Star veils the distance: ask a local about the pass ahead.
div.ziwei.result.26: The Jewel Star enriches the road palace: a small treasure comes with the journey.
div.ziwei.result.27: The Famine Star empties the market: sell before you arrive, not after.
div.ziwei.result.28: The Messenger Star brings word: a letter overtakes you at the relay station.
div.ziwei.result.29: The Ancient Star guards the end: the road's end holds a quiet reward.
end.cartographer.epilogue: {years} years and {cities} cities, and what you have to show is paper. The road from {longestRoute} is drawn to the day's march, with the water marked and the passes named. Others will use it and not know you. That is what a chart is for, and you knew it when you began.
end.cartographer.name: The Chart-Maker
end.diviner.epilogue: {cities} cities in {years} years, and in each of them you asked the same question in a different language. The stalks, the sticks, the cards and the stars do not agree, and you came to think that the disagreement is the answer. You keep {faith}, and you keep the others' methods too, which the learned of every city told you was impossible.
end.diviner.name: Reader of the Signs
end.lay_down.epilogue: You set out from {start} and you are stopping at {lastCity}: {cities} cities, {years} years, {faith} still, and {richestTrade} the best bargain you ever struck. The book ends because you have closed it, not because the road did. There is more of it. There was always going to be more of it.
end.lay_down.name: Laying Down the Pen
end.markets.epilogue: {years} years, {cities} cities, and a ledger that balances. You learned the thing the guidebooks cannot teach: that the same bale is two different goods in two places, and the distance between them is the whole of the profit. {richestTrade} was the making of you. You could name the day you understood it, and you never told anyone.
end.markets.name: Master of a Hundred Markets
end.no_return.epilogue: You crossed {cities} cities in {years} years and never came back to {start}. Some say you were last seen at {lastCity}; some say you died on the road. Both are true: a traveller's home is being spoken of, again and again.
end.no_return.name: The One Who Did Not Return
end.returned.epilogue: You came home to {start} after {years} years and {cities} cities, and found that the hardest part was the telling. Men who had never left the parish argued with you about the width of rivers. Of everything you carried back, it was {richestTrade} that made your fortune, and no one asked about it twice. The rest they did not believe, and you wrote it down anyway.
end.returned.name: The One Who Came Back
end.stayed.epilogue: You went out for a season and remained {years} years. {cities} cities are behind you and you are still at {lastCity}, which you no longer call by the name you learned it under. You keep {faith} as you always did, in a place that has its own arrangements about such things and does not press you. Venice is a word you can still spell.
end.stayed.name: The One Who Stayed
end.witness.epilogue: {cities} cities in {years} years, and the road from {longestRoute} the longest of them. You did not go as an envoy, and you did not go to trade; you went to see, and you saw. What you can report is small beside what there was: the tide of a river at a particular hour, the price of salt in a town with no name in any book. It is what a witness has.
end.witness.name: Witness of the World
ending.returned-to-venice.body: After {years} years on the road, you have returned to the city where you began. The Piazza San Marco is smaller than you remembered. The merchants who once seemed rich are now modest traders with modest horizons. Your cargo — {goods} — makes you the wealthiest man in Venice, but wealth no longer interests you. In the evenings, you stand on the Rialto and watch the ships you will never board, their holds full of pepper you no longer need to buy, bound for ports you have already seen. The Doge invites you to dinner; you tell the story of the {cities} cities you have passed through, and no one believes half of it. {faith} has taught you that the journey was the destination. The book you write will be called a fantasy. You will let them believe that.
ending.returned-to-venice.name: The Return
ending.stayed-in-the-east.body: You never went back. Somewhere on the {longestRoute} — the longest road you ever rode — you realised that the traveller you had become no longer belonged in the place that made you. You settled in {cities}, a city of {faith} prayers and merchants who speak {languages} languages. You took a local name. You married. Your children speak a tongue you learned as an adult. At night, when the traders arrive from the west, you listen to news of your birthplace the way you once listened to tales of Cathay — as a story about a country you have visited but no longer live in. In your old age, a young traveller arrives from Venice, full of questions. You answer none of them. Instead, you pour him tea and tell him about the road ahead.
ending.stayed-in-the-east.name: The East
ending.template: After {years} years of travel, you have seen {cities} cities. You crossed {deserts} deserts and sailed {seas} seas. The {longestRoute} taught you the most. {faith} sustained you when nothing else would. This is the story of how you became {final_title} — a name the road gave you, and the road will remember.
ending.witness-of-the-world.body: You have seen {cities} cities, crossed {deserts} deserts, and sailed {seas} seas. Your maps are the most accurate in the world, though only you can read them. Your journals fill a chest — prices, routes, customs, warnings, drawings of plants no physician has described, star-charts no astrologer has drawn. You are not the richest man in the world, nor the most powerful, but you are its greatest witness. When the scholars of {faith} come to interview you in your last years, you dictate for hours, days, weeks, until your voice gives out. They write it all down. The book they produce will be read for a hundred years, and every traveller who follows will follow your footsteps — whether they know your name or not. This is the only immortality that means anything: the road remembers.
ending.witness-of-the-world.name: The Witness
era.1253.description: The year of Rubruck's eastward journey: steppe diplomacy and post roads are still being remade.
era.1253.name: 1253 · Road to the khan's court
era.1292.description: The closing years of Polo's journey: transcontinental trade is rich in both witness and hearsay.
era.1292.name: 1292 · Roads between worlds
era.1325.description: The year Battuta left home: pilgrimage, scholarship and sea roads form one network.
era.1325.name: 1325 · Pilgrimage and sea roads
era.1405.description: The first Zheng He voyage: Indian Ocean ports enter a new diplomatic rhythm.
era.1405.name: 1405 · First treasure voyage
ev.accon.battuta_a.body: From Acre you ride to Tyre, ringed on three sides by the sea. At Kark Nuh lies the tomb of Abu Yaakūb Yusūf, said to have been a king of the west, with a cell endowed by Salāh Oddīn. They say he lived by weaving mats and kept orchards in Damascus for the sultan Nūr Oddīn; asked for pomegranates, he brought one after another seeming sour, answering: I was hired to keep the orchard, not to eat the pomegranates. And this is the wonder told of him: he gathered the copper furniture of a maiden's dower, fused it in a fire, touched it with elixir, and the whole became pure gold, with which Nūr Oddīn built the infirmary of Damascus.
ev.accon.battuta_a.choice.mat: Ask the tomb-keeper for the tale of the mat-weaver
ev.accon.battuta_a.choice.tomb: Visit the tomb of Abu Yaakūb at Kark Nuh
ev.accon.battuta_a.title: Copper Turned to Gold
ev.accon.entry.body: Acre upon the Syrian shore — a great haven of the Franks on this coast. Pilgrims and Maghribī merchants come down from Damascus to seek passage here; the tithe is taken at the mole, a qīrāt in every dīnār of goods. Venetian and Genoese galleys unload woolens and take on spicery for the return. Between Acre and Jerusalem lie three days; the plain about the walls has no gardens, and fruit is brought in from the hill farms. You must know that Latin, Greek, and Arabic tongues are all heard upon these quays, and that the Templars' tower watches the roadstead.
ev.accon.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.accon.entry.title: Arriving at Accon
ev.aden.a.body: You stand upon the quay where the great ships of India discharge their cargoes into lighter craft. Men say the pepper and spicery must pass seven days by sea to a lesser haven, then thirty days by camel to the river of Alexandria, whence it descends to that city. No road of equal convenience serves the merchants of Egypt. The bales are weighed, marked, and stacked in sheds that smell of clove and ginger.
ev.aden.a.choice.ask-routes: Ask the camel-masters which roads leave the harbour
ev.aden.a.choice.buy-pepper: Buy a sack of Malabar pepper for the onward road
ev.aden.a.choice.walk: Walk the sheds and watch the lighters load
ev.aden.a.title: The Pepper Lighters and the Camel Road
ev.aden.b.body: Above the harbour rises the Soldan's mosque, where the Saracens of Aden gather at the hours of prayer. Below it, the customs clerks take their due on every bale that crosses the mole — a tenth on pepper, a fee on cloth and dates. The harbour-master keeps a register in Arabic script; no ship departs without his seal. You mark how the muezzin's call and the clerks' abacus share the same wind off the sea.
ev.aden.b.choice.listen-prayer: Listen at the mosque door as the Soldan's men pray
ev.aden.b.choice.observe: Stand aside and observe the customs at the mole
ev.aden.b.choice.pay-frankincense: Pay the harbour fee and buy frankincense from a Somali trader
ev.aden.b.title: The Soldan's Mosque and the Harbour Customs
ev.aden.entry.body: You must know that in the province of ADEN there is a Prince who is called the Soldan. The people are all Saracens and adorers of Mahommet, and have a great hatred of Christians. There are many towns and villages in the country. This Aden is the port to which many of the ships of India come with their cargoes; and from this haven the merchants carry the goods a distance of seven days further in small vessels. At the end of those seven days they land the goods and load them on camels, and so carry them a land journey of 30 days. This brings them to the river of ALEXANDRIA, and by it they descend to the latter city. It is by this way through Aden that the Saracens of Alexandria receive all their stores of pepper and other spicery; and there is no other route equally good and convenient by which these goods could reach that place.
ev.aden.entry.choice.pass: Pass through the darvāzā without delay
ev.aden.entry.title: Concerning the Province of Aden
ev.alexandria.battuta_a.body: At evening the keeper of Alexandria's gate is impatient to close it, for a poor scholar sits near the gate and will not enter until he has seen some favourable omen. He came from the Hejaz poor, and as all the travellers go in and it is nearly time to close, the keeper cries to him in irony: Enter, Mr Judge. He answers: Yes, judge, if that be God's will. He enters one of the colleges, and attends to reading so diligently that his name and modesty reach the king of Egypt. When the judge of Alexandria dies, many learned men of the city expect the appointment — the scholar expects nothing, and the sultan sends it to him.
ev.alexandria.battuta_a.choice.observe: Stand by the gate as the keeper jests
ev.alexandria.battuta_a.choice.omen: Mark the omen and enter as he did
ev.alexandria.battuta_a.choice.speak: Ask the scholar why he will not enter
ev.alexandria.battuta_a.title: A Judge Named at the Gate
ev.alexandria.battuta_b.body: One of the greatest saints of Alexandria is the learned and pious Imam Borhāna Oddīn El Aaraj, a worker of miracles. You go in to him, and he says: I perceive that you are fond of travelling into various countries. You say yes, though you have no intention of travelling into very distant parts. He replies: You must visit my brother Farīd Oddīn in India, my brother Rokn Oddīn Ibn Zakaryā in Sind, and my brother Borhān Oddīn in China, and when you see them, present my compliments to them. You are astonished at his words, and determine to visit those countries; nor do you give up the purpose till you have met all the three and presented his compliments.
ev.alexandria.battuta_b.choice.ask: Ask the names of the three brothers
ev.alexandria.battuta_b.choice.depart: Take leave with the prophecy in your journal
ev.alexandria.battuta_b.choice.promise: Swear to carry the saint's greetings east
ev.alexandria.battuta_b.title: The Saint's Prophecy of Three Brothers
ev.alexandria.entry.body: You come into Alexandria by the sea-gate of Misr, and the first thing you mark is the weighing of bales. The Sultan's clerks take their tamghā on every pack that leaves the quay — pepper of India, glass of Syria, grain of Egypt, woolens of the Franks. The old light-tower that once guided ships from every sea is a ruin; its stones have gone into the walls. And yet the harbours still teem, and learned men keep cells in this city — imāms and sheikhs whose names are known from Sindia to China. You must know that no junk puts in here without passing beneath the clerks' brushes, and no traveller leaves without hearing what the saints of this place have said of the road ahead.
ev.alexandria.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.alexandria.entry.title: Arriving at Alexandria
ev.alexandria.mentor_geomancy.body: Near the warehouses a geomancer casts for risk on the sea lanes and the desert posts alike.
ev.alexandria.mentor_geomancy.choice.ask: Ask what Populus means for a voyage
ev.alexandria.mentor_geomancy.title: Sand by the Pharos road
ev.antiochia.entry.body: You come down to Antioch upon the river El Aāsī, which the men of Hamah call the Rebel. The town sits under the mountains of the frontier, between Muslim lands and the castles of the Franks that once held this coast. Within the walls is the tomb of Habīb El Najār, which pilgrims visit; beyond, toward the high places, lie the fortresses of the Ismāīlīah — Bugrās, El Shaghar, Masyāf, El Kahf — and no stranger walks freely among them. Caravans still pass the Orontes bridge with silk and steel; the Sultan's watch holds the gates. You must know that this was once among the great cities of the Romans, and men still speak of it as they speak of old Damascus.
ev.antiochia.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.antiochia.entry.title: Arriving at Antiochia
ev.axuma.entry.body: You come into Axum by the highland road, where the air is thin and the stone of the old stelae catches the sun. This was once a Christian kingdom that traded ivory and gold to the Red Sea — you must know that its kings struck coin and sent embassies as far as Constantinople. The Church still prays in Ge'ez within walls of cut stone; the obelisks stand crooked but unbroken. Yet Aden and the Yemeni ports have drawn the sea-trade away, and the bāzār shows more dust than silk. Pilgrims and a few caravans still pause here for water and for the blessing of the priests.
ev.axuma.entry.choice.rest: Rest half a day by the road
ev.axuma.entry.title: Arriving at Axuma
ev.babylonia-cairus.entry.body: Misr and Cairo stand upon the Nile, one city and yet two — the old settlement of Fustāt and the new quarters under the citadel. Four congregational mosques of superb build rise among many lesser ones; the mosque of ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ās draws a daily income for its readers and imāms. Theological colleges throughout Misr and Cairo are maintained by the Sultan's bounty — two thousand Egyptian dīnārs a month, men say. Villages and towns follow continuously along the river. You must know that this is the seat of Ayyubid power in Egypt, and that no stranger lodges long without hearing the Friday khutbah in the Sunni manner.
ev.babylonia-cairus.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.babylonia-cairus.entry.title: Arriving at Babylonia Cairus
ev.badashan.a.body: You climb to the highland bāzār where rough lapis lazuli and balas rubies change hands under the king's seal. The stones are dug in great caves among the mountains — men say only the mountain of Syghinan yields the rubies, and that none may carry them beyond the kingdom on pain of forfeiture. Brokers weigh each block on brass scales and murmur prices in a tongue you scarcely follow.
ev.badashan.a.choice.ask-mines: Ask where the ruby mines lie in the mountains
ev.badashan.a.choice.buy-lapis: Buy a block of raw lapis lazuli
ev.badashan.a.choice.walk: Walk among the stone brokers and listen to their bargaining
ev.badashan.a.title: The Lapis and Balas Ruby Trade
ev.badashan.b.body: In the audience hall of Badashan you hear how every prince of the royal blood claims descent from Alexander and the daughter of Darius, Lord of Persia. They call themselves Zulcarniaim in the Saracen tongue — that is to say, Alexander — out of reverence for the great conqueror. The common folk speak a mountain tongue unlike any Arabic or Persian you have heard on the plains. A court scribe writes your name in their script and smiles at your puzzlement.
ev.badashan.b.choice.buy-ruby: Buy a small balas ruby from a licensed broker
ev.badashan.b.choice.learn-tongue: Pay a scribe to teach you a few words of the mountain tongue
ev.badashan.b.choice.listen: Listen as the court herald recites the royal genealogy
ev.badashan.b.title: The Royal Lineage and the Mountain Tongue
ev.badashan.entry.body: Badashan is a Province inhabited by people who worship Mahommet, and have a peculiar language. It forms a very great kingdom, and the royalty is hereditary. All those of the royal blood are descended from King Alexander and the daughter of King Darius, who was Lord of the vast Empire of Persia. And all these kings call themselves in the Saracen tongue ZULCARNIAIN, which is as much as to say _Alexander_; and this out of regard for Alexander the Great. It is in this province that those fine and valuable gems the Balas Rubies are found. They are got in certain rocks among the mountains, and in the search for them the people dig great caves underground, just as is done by miners for silver. There is but one special mountain that produces them, and it is called SYGHINAN. The stones are dug on the king’s account, and no one else dares dig in that mountain on pain of forfeiture of life as well as goods; nor may any one carry the stones out of the kingdom.
ev.badashan.entry.choice.pass: Pass through the darvāzeh without delay
ev.badashan.entry.title: Of the Province of Badashan
ev.balc.a.body: Balc was once the mother of cities — the capital of Bactria, where Alexander the Great took Roxana of Sogdiana as his bride. Its walls enclosed more ground than any city in Asia, and its temples held treasure from India, Persia, and Greece. Now its broken ramparts, collapsed domes, and empty palaces tell the same story as every city east of the Oxus: the Mongol rider came, and nothing was left standing. Yet the caravans still stop here, and the city is slowly rebuilding from the rubble. The new houses are smaller, built from the stones of the old, but the market is alive again. The King of Balc pays tribute to the Great Kaan, and the trade of lapis lazuli, rubies, and Turkoman horses keeps the city's heart beating.
ev.balc.a.choice.explore: Search the ruins where Alexander married Roxana
ev.balc.a.choice.fragment: Pick up a carved stone from the old city
ev.balc.a.choice.listen: Ask an old man what this city was in its height
ev.balc.a.title: The Ruins of Bactra
ev.balc.b.body: The caravanserai of Balc is one of the largest on the Silk Road — a fortress-sized courtyard ringed with stables for a thousand camels, storerooms stacked with bales of silk and leather sacks of lapis, and chambers for merchants of every nation. Lapis lazuli from the mines of Badakhshan, which lies twelve days east, is the city's chief treasure; it is sold in rough blocks and traded for silver, silk, and spices. Balas rubies from the mountains fetch prices that would buy a ship in Venice. Horses from the Turkoman plains are auctioned in the inner courtyard. The caravanserai never sleeps; fires burn in the arcades all night, and the smell of lamb kebab and saffron rice hangs in the air.
ev.balc.b.choice.lapis: Buy a block of raw lapis lazuli from Badakhshan
ev.balc.b.choice.ruby: Buy a balas ruby — worth a ship in Venice
ev.balc.b.choice.talk_traders: Ask the caravan masters where the roads go
ev.balc.b.title: The Caravanserai of Balc
ev.balc.c.body: On a hill outside the city, a fire-temple of the ancient Persian faith still burns — the Magi tend a flame they say has never been extinguished since the days of Zoroaster, a thousand years before the Prophet. The people call it the Tomb of the Magi, and they say that the three wise men who visited the infant Christ are buried here, in three stone sarcophagi that still bear traces of gold leaf. Pilgrims from Persia, India, and even distant Cathay climb the hill to leave offerings of incense and silver coins. The Magi in their white robes chant the ancient hymns at dawn and dusk. They say that a man who sleeps at the shrine will dream of his own death — and that every dream they have recorded has come true.
ev.balc.c.choice.chant: Listen to the Magi chant at dawn
ev.balc.c.choice.offering: Leave incense at the fire that has never gone out
ev.balc.c.choice.sleep: Sleep at the Tomb of the Magi and wait for a dream
ev.balc.c.title: The Shrine of the Magi
ev.balc.entry.body: Balc is a noble city and a great, though it was much greater in former days. But the Tartars and other nations have greatly ravaged and destroyed it. There were formerly many fine palaces and buildings of marble, and the ruins of them still remain. The people of the city tell that it was here that Alexander took to wife the daughter of Darius. Here, you should be told, is the end of the empire of the Tartar Lord of the Levant. And this city is also the limit of Persia in the direction between east and north-east. Now, let us quit this city, and I will tell you of another country called DOGANA. When you have quitted the city of which I have been speaking, you ride some 12 days between north-east and east, without finding any human habitation, for the people have all taken refuge in fastnesses among the mountains, on account of the Banditti and armies that harassed them. There is plenty of water on the road, and abundance of game; there are lions too. You can get no provisions on the road, and must carry with you all that you require for these 12 days.
ev.balc.entry.choice.customs: Declare your goods at the bājgāh (toll-house)
ev.balc.entry.choice.lore: Ask what men say of this city
ev.balc.entry.title: Of the City of Balc
ev.balc.mentor_closure.body: Before you leave Balc, the old copyist of the lapis road asks what you have learned from Balc. The lesson is not a spell or a bargain; it is a way of noticing which detail will matter after the road turns.
ev.balc.mentor_closure.choice_1: Ask what the road will demand
ev.balc.mentor_closure.choice_1_result: The copyist answers without evasion: tolls, dry stages, and the reading of men will be asked of you. His lesson is offered, and what you make of it lies with you.
ev.balc.mentor_closure.choice_2: Stay for a day and listen to the whole account
ev.balc.mentor_closure.choice_2_result: You stay a day at the copyist's table, and he sets the whole account before you at leisure. What he reads aloud is longer than the parting lesson, and it earns what it asks.
ev.balc.mentor_closure.choice_3: Thank the guide and keep moving
ev.balc.mentor_closure.choice_3_result: You thank the old copyist and take the road. He lets you go with a blessing, and the lesson of Balc remains unwritten.
ev.balc.mentor_closure.title: The Guide of Balc
ev.baldacum.a.body: The great palace of the Caliph of Baghdad covered more ground than any building in Islam. Its golden dome could be seen three days' journey away across the flat plain of the Tigris. Within were halls hung with silk embroidered with gold thread, gardens watered by channels drawn from the river, courtyards paved with marble brought from every corner of the Caliphate, and the treasury that held the tribute of a hundred nations. The Caliph himself was never seen except by a handful of servants and his vizier. His harem contained a thousand women; his guard was an army of twenty thousand Turkic slaves. And yet when Hulagu came to the walls, all that gold and all those swords could not save him.
ev.baldacum.a.choice.explore: Explore the ruined halls of the Caliph
ev.baldacum.a.choice.listen: Hire a guard to tell you what this place once was
ev.baldacum.a.choice.treasure: Bribe the old warden and search the treasury rubble
ev.baldacum.a.title: The Caliph's Palace
ev.baldacum.b.body: Merchants from India, Persia, Syria, and the Levant crowd the covered markets of Baudas. The bazaars are organized by trade — the silversmiths in one vaulted lane, the silk-merchants in another, the spice-sellers in a third — and each guild maintains its own mosque, bathhouse, and coffee-house. Silk and cloth of gold from Mosul, spices from Hormuz and India, pearls from the Gulf, paper from Samarcand, and Damascus steel blades change hands by the hour. The money-changers sit cross-legged behind low tables covered with mountains of silver dirhams; the merchants drink sherbet cooled with snow brought down from the Kurdish mountains and argue over fractions of a grain of gold.
ev.baldacum.b.choice.brocade: Buy a length of Baghdad brocade worked with gold
ev.baldacum.b.choice.sherbet: Drink sherbet with the money-changers and listen
ev.baldacum.b.choice.spices: Ask the spice-sellers where their wares come from
ev.baldacum.b.title: The Bazaars of Baudas
ev.baldacum.c.body: The story of how Hulagu took this city is still told in the bazaars. The Caliph, trusting in his gold and his twenty thousand guards, refused to pay tribute to the Great Khan and defied the Mongol envoy. Hulagu marched on the city with a host that blackened the plain from horizon to horizon. He broke the dikes of the Tigris and flooded the Mongol camp, but his engineers diverted the water and drained the Caliph's moat. When the walls fell, Hulagu shut the Caliph in his own treasury — a tower full of gold, silver, jewels, and silk — and told him to eat his treasure. The Caliph starved among his wealth, and the city burned for a month.
ev.baldacum.c.choice.listen: Hear the full tale of how Hulagu took the city
ev.baldacum.c.choice.record: Write down the story while it is still told
ev.baldacum.c.choice.search: Search for a coin from before the sack
ev.baldacum.c.title: The Fall of the City
ev.baldacum.entry.body: Baudas is a great city, which used to be the seat of the Calif of all the Saracens in the world, just as Rome is the seat of the Pope of all the Christians. A very great river flows through the city, and by this you can descend to the Sea of India. There is a great traffic of merchants with their goods this way; they descend some eighteen days from Baudas, and then come to a certain city called KISI, where they enter the Sea of India. There is also on the river, as you go from Baudas to Kisi, a great city called BASTRA, surrounded by woods, in which grow the best dates in the world. In Baudas they weave many different kinds of silk stuffs and gold brocades, such as _nasich_, and _nac_, and _cramoisy_, and many another beautiful tissue richly wrought with figures of beasts and birds. It is the noblest and greatest city in all those regions. Now it came to pass on a day in the year of Christ 1255, that the Lord of the Tartars of the Levant, whose name was Alaü, brother to the Great Kaan now reigning, gathered a mighty host and came up against Baudas and took it by storm. It was a great enterprise! for in Baudas there were more than 100,000 horse, besides foot soldiers. And when Alaü had taken the place he found therein a tower of the Califs, which was full of gold and silver and other treasure; in fact the greatest accumulation of treasure in one spot that ever was known. When he beheld that great heap of treasure he was astonished, and, summoning the Calif to his presence, he said to him: “Calif, tell me now why thou hast gathered such a huge treasure? What didst thou mean to do therewith? Knewest thou not that I was thine enemy, and that I was coming against thee with so great an host to cast thee forth of thine heritage? Wherefore didst thou not take of thy gear and employ it in paying knights and soldiers to defend thee and thy city?” The Calif wist not what to answer, and said never a word.
ev.baldacum.entry.choice.customs: Declare your goods at the tamghā-khāna (tax-house)
ev.baldacum.entry.choice.lore: Ask what men say of this city
ev.baldacum.entry.title: Of the Great City of Baudas, and How It Was Taken
ev.baldacum.geomancy_court.body: Dust is drawn into a figure for the road you mean to take today.
ev.baldacum.geomancy_court.title: Sand before the Court Gate
ev.baldacum.mentor_bazi.body: A calendar master will teach four pillars to read three-year travel windows.
ev.baldacum.mentor_bazi.choice.ask: Ask how calendars serve the road
ev.baldacum.mentor_bazi.choice.learn_geo: Pay and learn the sand figures as well
ev.baldacum.mentor_bazi.title: Pillars at Baghdad
ev.baldacum.mentor_geomancy.body: A sand-reader marks sixteen figures in the dust and teaches which open a road, which stop it, and which hold you a day. He will speak of great fortune and great ill omen without shame — the sand does.
ev.baldacum.mentor_geomancy.title: Sand in Baldacum
ev.basora.entry.body: Basra stands where the waters of Irāk run down toward the Gulf. You travel hither with the Badawīn of Khafāja, for there is no safe going in these parts except in their company. Date-palms line the canals; gardens and plastered walls mark the richer houses. Upstream lie Wāsit and the shrines of Meshhed Alī, where the Shīah keep their treasury of vows; down the river the dhows take dates, grain, and cloth toward Omān and India. You must know that Basra has been a gate of the sea since the first centuries of Islam, and that its markets still speak Arabic, Persian, and the tongues of the Gulf.
ev.basora.entry.choice.rest: Rest half a day by the road
ev.basora.entry.title: Arriving at Basora
ev.berrhoea.entry.body: Aleppo — Haleb — is a town of eminent consequence; its fame has flown high in all ages. The fortress is renowned for impregnability and is seen from far off for its height. Markets and streets are broad; the highest markets are roofed, their shops as large as khāns. Within the citadel is a meshhed where Abraham is said to have performed his devotions. The road hither passes al-Bāb, where the Ismā‘īlīyah once held the gate between Buza‘ah and the city. You must know that Aleppo has been sought by many kings, and that its roofed sūqs and its citadel mark it among the great cities of Syria.
ev.berrhoea.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.berrhoea.entry.title: Arriving at Berrhoea
ev.bethleem.entry.body: You climb from Jerusalem by a short, steep road of white stone and come to Bethlehem on its hill — a small town, yet holy to Christians as the birthplace of the Lord. Pilgrims throng the Grotto of the Nativity; candles smoke against the rock, and the Latin and Eastern rites keep their hours in turn. You must know that the monasteries here offer bread, olives, and a pallet to any traveller who asks in the name of charity. Olive terraces ring the slopes; shepherds still drive flocks as they did in the old accounts. From the ridge you may see the Dead Sea haze to the east, and the road back to Jerusalem glittering in the afternoon light.
ev.bethleem.entry.choice.rest: Rest half a day by the road
ev.bethleem.entry.title: Arriving at Bethleem
ev.bochara.battuta_a.body: Bokhāra, the principal city of the country beyond the Gihon, was ravaged by the Tartars until it almost entirely disappeared; no one there knows anything of science. It is said that Jengiz Khān, who came with the Tartars and destroyed the countries of Islam, began as a blacksmith in the country of Khotā — liberal-minded, powerful, and corpulent. He assembled and feasted the people, who joined him and made him their leader. He conquered his district, then all Khotā, then China, then Khashak, Kāshgar, and Mālik. For an affair among merchants, in which property had been taken, he invaded the lands of Jalāl Oddīn Sanjar, king of Khavārezm, and put his army to the rout.
ev.bochara.battuta_a.choice.melon: Buy dried Bokhāra melons for the road
ev.bochara.battuta_a.choice.ruins: Search the ruined streets for any remnant of learning
